items.note: A time word here. Not the まえ (mae) from Lesson 12, which means "in front" and is a place. After a verb, as in たべるまえに (taberu mae ni), it means "before doing it".
The verb before まえに (mae ni) stays in the dictionary form from Lesson 15, not the ます-form: たべるまえに (taberu mae ni), never たべますまえに.
Drop ます (masu) from たべます (tabemasu) and add たいです (tai desu). The ます-stem is what carries the ending.
Same pattern: the dictionary form ねる (neru) plus まえに (mae ni), not ねます (nemasu).

items.note: Contrast しつれいします (shitsurei shimasu), also "Good-bye." from Frequently Used Expressions, and じゃ、また (ja, mata) "See you." Those cover leaving an office or a casual parting, while さようなら (sayōnara) is the plain farewell.
Literally "again tomorrow"; じゃ、また + a time word is the usual parting phrase, e.g. じゃ、また すいようびに.
たい (tai) then behaves like an い-adjective: it becomes たくない (takunai), like おおきい (ōkii) to おおきくないです (ōkikunai desu) from Lesson 11.
Past follows the い-adjective pattern too: たい (tai) becomes たかった (takatta), like たのしい (tanoshii) to たのしかったです (tanoshikatta desu) from Lesson 11.
